project.name: 3D-HomeVerse
project.description: A 3D interior design web application with a custom ECS engine, dual 2D/3D view, and React-based UI.

nodes.name: AmbientLightComponent.ts
nodes.summary: ECS component data bag representing an ambient light, storing color and intensity values used by LightSystem to create and sync Three.js AmbientLight objects.

nodes.name: AmbientLightComponent
nodes.summary: Component holding ambient light parameters (color, intensity) with sensible defaults; extends the ECS Component base class.

nodes.name: DirectionalLightComponent.ts
nodes.summary: ECS component data bag for a directional light, capturing color, intensity, and full shadow-map configuration including camera size and bias tuned for residential-scale scenes.
nodes.languageNotes: Shadow camera size is intentionally set to 25 (covering 50x50m) to fit typical residential floor plans, with inline comments explaining the tradeoff.

nodes.name: DirectionalLightComponent
nodes.summary: Component storing directional light properties plus shadow map settings (mapSize, camera size, bias) with defaults calibrated for a 50x50m orthographic shadow volume.

nodes.name: Grounded.ts
nodes.summary: Minimal ECS component marking an entity as subject to ground-clamping physics, tracking grounded state and a coyote-time counter for jump-leniency logic.

nodes.name: Grounded
nodes.summary: Component that flags an entity as grounded and tracks coyote-timer state for forgiving ground detection.

nodes.name: LightHandle.ts
nodes.summary: ECS component that holds a reference to a live Three.js Light object, bridging the ECS data layer to the Three.js scene graph for LightSystem.

nodes.name: LightHandle
nodes.summary: Component wrapping a THREE.Light reference so ECS systems can update the Three.js object without querying the scene graph directly.

nodes.name: Transform.ts
nodes.summary: Core ECS component storing 3D position and orientation as a quaternion (x,y,z,w), with convenience yaw getter/setter and a full setQuaternion helper used by the Gizmo system.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a quaternion as the canonical rotation representation matching Three.js and cannon-es conventions; the rotY property provides a yaw-only view for 2D placement and wall tools.

nodes.name: Transform
nodes.summary: Component storing world-space position (x,y,z) and a quaternion rotation with a rotY yaw accessor and setQuaternion for full 3-axis rotation support.

nodes.name: Query.ts
nodes.summary: Provides the ECS Query utility with an optimized static method that returns entity IDs matching all required component types, using a pivot-on-smallest-set strategy for O(smallestSet × types) performance.

nodes.name: Query
nodes.summary: Static-method utility class for querying entities by component composition; pivots on the component type with the fewest registered entities to minimize iteration.

nodes.name: System.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the abstract System base class for the ECS engine, declaring the per-frame update(world, deltaTime) contract that all concrete systems must implement.

nodes.name: System
nodes.summary: Abstract ECS System base class providing a no-op default update() that concrete systems override to process entities each frame.

nodes.name: World.ts
nodes.summary: Core ECS World container managing entity lifecycle, sparse component storage (Map-of-Maps), system registration, and the per-frame update loop; also exposes a revision counter for change detection.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a sparse-matrix layout (Map<ComponentClass, Map<entityId, Component>>) providing O(1) component lookup and enabling Query to pivot on the smallest component set.

nodes.name: World
nodes.summary: The central ECS World class — creates/destroys entities, attaches/detaches components, registers systems, drives the per-frame update loop, and tracks a revision counter for snapshot invalidation.

nodes.name: GroundSystem.ts
nodes.summary: ECS System that clamps entities with both a Transform and Grounded component to the y=0 floor plane each frame, setting isGrounded when contact is detected.

nodes.name: GroundSystem
nodes.summary: System querying Transform+Grounded entities and enforcing a fake floor at y=0 by clamping position and setting the grounded flag.

nodes.name: LightSystem.ts
nodes.summary: ECS System that lazily creates Three.js AmbientLight and DirectionalLight objects (with full shadow configuration) for entities carrying the corresponding light components, then keeps them synchronized each frame.

nodes.name: LightSystem
nodes.summary: System that bridges ECS light component data to Three.js scene graph lights — instantiating lights on first encounter and syncing color, intensity, and position every frame.

nodes.name: update
nodes.summary: Per-frame update that processes ambient and directional light entities — lazily creating Three.js lights with full shadow map setup and synchronizing their properties from ECS component data.

nodes.name: update
nodes.summary: Per-frame update that iterates grounded entities and clamps their y-position to 0, setting the isGrounded flag when floor contact occurs.

nodes.name: entitiesWith
nodes.summary: Static method returning entity IDs that possess every listed component type, using a pivot-on-smallest-set optimization to minimize iteration cost.

nodes.name: DrawWallTool.tsx
nodes.summary: Implements the interactive wall-drawing tool for the 2D floor plan editor, handling mouse input, snap logic, collision detection against placed furniture, and Konva overlay rendering for the preview segment.

nodes.name: DrawWallTool
nodes.summary: Tool class that manages the wall-drawing workflow: tracks drawing state, snaps cursor to grid/nodes/angle constraints, blocks placement when the preview segment collides with existing furniture, and dispatches ECS commands to commit walls.

nodes.name: PlaceFurnitureTool.tsx
nodes.summary: Implements the ghost-preview furniture placement tool for the 2D floor plan, displaying a top-down image of the selected furniture piece and blocking placement when the OBB ghost collides with walls or other furniture.

nodes.name: PlaceFurnitureTool
nodes.summary: Tool class that tracks a furniture ghost at cursor position, snaps to a 0.25 m grid, recomputes OBB collision on every move, and dispatches a PLACE_FURNITURE command on confirmed click; right-click or Escape cancels placement.

nodes.name: SelectTool.tsx
nodes.summary: Implements the selection and drag-editing tool for walls and wall-node handles in the 2D floor plan, supporting click-to-select, drag-to-move nodes, and transactional ECS command dispatch.

nodes.name: SelectTool
nodes.summary: Tool class implementing wall selection (click-toggle, deselect on empty-stage click) and drag-move for individual wall nodes, using snap-to-node and transactional dispatch to keep the ECS consistent.

nodes.name: ToolBase.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the ToolBase interface and ToolContext/WallHandlers type contracts that all 2D editor tools must implement, establishing the push-down context pattern where the host (PlanView2D) injects fresh data each render cycle.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure TypeScript type/interface file with no runtime code; exports WallHandlers, ToolContext, and the ToolBase interface. The push-context pattern avoids stale closures in Konva event handlers.

nodes.name: collision2D.ts
nodes.summary: Provides SAT-based (Separating Axis Theorem) 2D collision detection utilities operating in Konva pixel-space, including OBB corner generation, wall-segment polygon construction, and overlap tests between furniture and walls.
nodes.languageNotes: All geometry runs in pixel-space (not world-space) to match Konva coordinates directly. A GAP_PX=0.5 tolerance prevents false positives from edge-touching objects.

nodes.name: obbCorners
nodes.summary: Computes the four corner vertices of a rotated bounding box (OBB) centered at (cx, cy) by applying a 2D rotation matrix to local half-extents, matching Konva's clockwise rotation convention.

nodes.name: wallSegmentPolygon
nodes.summary: Constructs a convex quad (4-vertex polygon) representing the pixel-space footprint of a wall segment with a given thickness, used as the collision shape for DrawWallTool preview checks.

nodes.name: collidesWithFurniture
nodes.summary: Tests whether a given convex polygon overlaps any furniture OBB in the scene (optionally ignoring one piece by ID), returning true on the first SAT intersection found.

nodes.name: collidesWithWalls
nodes.summary: Tests whether a given convex polygon overlaps any wall segment polygon in the scene using SAT, used by PlaceFurnitureTool to block ghost placement that intersects walls.

nodes.name: polygonsIntersect
nodes.summary: Core SAT implementation that tests two convex polygons for overlap by projecting both onto all edge-normal axes and checking for separating gaps.

nodes.name: toolUtils.ts
nodes.summary: Exports shared geometry constants (pixel-per-world scale, wall thickness, snap radii, angle snap angles) and pure utility functions (coordinate conversion, node/grid snapping, angle snapping) used by all 2D editor tools.
nodes.languageNotes: Entirely pure functions with no React or Konva imports; snap priority order is node snap → wall projection snap → grid snap.

nodes.name: snapToNodeOrGrid
nodes.summary: Resolves a raw pixel cursor position to a snapped position using a three-tier priority: snap to nearby node, then project onto the nearest wall segment, then fall back to grid rounding.

nodes.name: applyAngleSnap
nodes.summary: Constrains the new wall direction to a set of canonical angles (multiples of 15/30/45/90°) relative to existing walls already connected at the anchor node, activating only when the cursor angle is within ANGLE_SNAP_THRESHOLD_DEG.

nodes.name: toWorldX
nodes.summary: Converts a pixel X coordinate (relative to the Konva stage) to a world-space X value by subtracting the viewport origin and dividing by PX_PER_WORLD.

nodes.name: toWorldZ
nodes.summary: Converts a pixel Y coordinate (relative to the Konva stage) to a world-space Z value by subtracting the viewport origin and dividing by PX_PER_WORLD.

nodes.summary: Top navigation bar for the editor that displays the app logo, a mode-aware label ('3D Editor' / 'Floor Plan'), and placeholder action icon buttons (Screenshot, Grid, Help) with hover animations.

nodes.name: components.md
nodes.summary: Placeholder documentation file in the components directory; currently empty, intended to document the component architecture of the editor UI.

nodes.name: BuildPanel.tsx
nodes.summary: Editor UI panel component for selecting wall types (Straight, Curved, Freehand) in the 2D floor plan builder, displayed as a floating bottom toolbar that animates in when the 'build' navigation tab is active.

nodes.name: BuildPanel
nodes.summary: React functional component rendering a floating bottom toolbar with wall-type selector buttons (Straight active, Curved/Freehand disabled as coming soon), with animated show/hide based on activeNav state.

nodes.name: Canvas.tsx
nodes.summary: React wrapper component for the Three.js WebGL canvas that initializes the engine via createEngine on mount, fires onEngineCreated for context propagation, and cleans up on unmount.

nodes.name: Canvas
nodes.summary: React functional component that mounts a full-viewport canvas element and bootstraps the Three.js engine via useEffect, notifying parent components through onEngineCreated and onReady callbacks.

nodes.name: DecorCatalog.tsx
nodes.summary: Full-screen modal catalog component for browsing and selecting decor/furniture items, featuring search, category filter chips, animated open/close transitions, keyboard Escape handling, and a staggered item grid rendered via the CatalogItem sub-component.

nodes.name: DecorCatalog
nodes.summary: Main exported React component implementing the decor catalog modal with controlled open/close animation state, search filtering, category chip filtering, and Escape key capture.

nodes.name: CatalogItem
nodes.summary: Internal sub-component rendering a single catalog card with hover animation, staggered CSS entrance delay, thumbnail image with fallback icon, and click handler that fires onSelect.

nodes.name: furnitureImages.ts
nodes.summary: Image loader and crop cache module for top-down furniture sprites, providing async load-on-demand, pixel-level alpha bounding box computation for tight cropping, and a subscriber notification system for React re-render triggers.

nodes.name: computeCrop
nodes.summary: Scans an image's alpha channel pixel-by-pixel via a temporary canvas to compute the tight opaque bounding box, falling back to full image dimensions if the canvas read fails or the image is fully transparent.

nodes.name: ensureImage
nodes.summary: Triggers an async image load for the given URL if not already cached, updating the shared image cache and notifying all subscribers upon load completion.

nodes.name: subscribeImages
nodes.summary: Registers a listener callback that is called whenever any furniture image finishes loading, returning an unsubscribe function for use as a React external store subscription.

nodes.name: furnitureSprite.tsx
nodes.summary: Provides the shared TopDownSprite Konva renderer for furniture top-down images used by both the placed-furniture layer (PlanView2D) and the placement ghost tool, applying alpha-crop and orientation correction so sprites fill footprints pixel-identically across both contexts.
nodes.languageNotes: Corrects PNG orientation by swapping width/depth and applying a -90 degree rotation when the sprite's long axis disagrees with the footprint's long axis.

nodes.name: TopDownSprite
nodes.summary: Renders a furniture top-down image as a Konva Image node centered on the parent Group origin, applying alpha-crop and a 90-degree rotation when the sprite orientation does not match the footprint orientation.

nodes.name: LoadingScreen.tsx
nodes.summary: Full-screen loading overlay displayed while the 3D engine initializes, featuring an animated progress bar, cycling status messages, logo, and a fade-out animation triggered when the engine is ready.

nodes.name: LoadingScreen
nodes.summary: Renders the full-screen loading overlay with a progress track, cycling status messages via setInterval, and CSS opacity-based fade-out when the done prop becomes true.

nodes.name: PlacementHint.tsx
nodes.summary: Floating tooltip displayed at the bottom of the screen while furniture placement mode is active, instructing the user to click to place or right-click/Escape to cancel.

nodes.name: PlanView2D.tsx
nodes.summary: The primary 2D floor plan canvas component built on Konva, responsible for rendering walls, rooms, furniture top-down views, dimension annotations, and handling all pan/zoom/selection/placement interactions via a layered Konva Stage and a tool delegation pattern.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements a 10-layer Konva Stage architecture (rooms, labels, wall outlines, wall fills, furniture, transformer, dimensions, angles, tool overlay, axes) with separate listening flags per layer to minimize hit-test overhead.

nodes.name: PlanView2D
nodes.summary: Main 2D floor plan rendering and interaction component that coordinates tool delegation, ECS data subscription via useFloorPlanStore, pan/zoom state, furniture selection/drag/rotate, and the WallPropertiesPanel.

nodes.name: renderFurnitureBody
nodes.summary: Renders a furniture item as either a PNG top-down sprite (TopDownSprite) when an image is loaded, or a gray rectangle with a modelId label as fallback.

nodes.name: SceneView3D.tsx
nodes.summary: Thin wrapper around the Canvas component for 3D view mode, forwarding onReady and onEngineCreated props so EditorPage does not directly depend on Canvas internals.

nodes.name: ShortcutHint.tsx
nodes.summary: Fixed-position keyboard shortcut reference panel rendered in the bottom-right corner of the editor, listing all active shortcut keys (V, B, F, M, R, Q, W, Tab) with their mode labels.

nodes.name: WallPropertiesPanel.tsx
nodes.summary: Side panel component for editing selected wall properties (thickness 75-300mm and height 2700-4500mm) with synchronized slider and number inputs, supporting multi-wall selection and dispatching UPDATE_WALL via an onApply callback.

nodes.name: WallPropertiesPanel
nodes.summary: Renders the wall properties editing panel with thickness and height sliders/inputs, syncing local state with initialThickness/Height props, and converting mm to world units (metres) before invoking onApply.

nodes.name: EngineContext.tsx
nodes.summary: Defines the React context that shares the EngineInstance across the component tree, providing both a safe nullable hook (useEngineOrNull) for components that render before engine initialization and a strict throwing hook (useEngine) for components that require a ready engine.

nodes.name: useEngineOrNull
nodes.summary: Safe hook that returns the EngineInstance from context or null if the engine is not yet initialized or no Provider is present.

nodes.name: useEngine
nodes.summary: Strict hook that throws an error if the engine is not found in context, intended for components that are guaranteed to render after engine initialization.

nodes.name: hooks.md
nodes.summary: Empty placeholder documentation file for the hooks directory.

nodes.name: useEngineDispatch.ts
nodes.summary: Custom hook that binds all engine API methods (dispatch, transaction management, ID generation) to the engine from EngineContext, returning stable-shaped functions that are safe no-ops when the engine has not yet initialized.

nodes.name: useEngineDispatch
nodes.summary: Returns an EngineDispatch object containing null-safe wrappers around engine.api methods for dispatch, transaction management (begin/commit/cancel), and ID allocation (nextNodeId, nextWallId).

nodes.name: usePlanShortcuts.ts
nodes.summary: Custom hook that registers and manages keyboard shortcuts for the 2D floor plan view, handling Delete/Backspace (remove walls/furniture), Ctrl+A (select all walls), Escape (cancel active tool), and Ctrl+Z/Y (undo/redo).

nodes.name: usePlanShortcuts
nodes.summary: Registers a keydown event listener that handles Delete/Backspace for entity deletion, Ctrl+A for wall select-all, Escape for tool cancel, and Ctrl+Z/Y for undo/redo, delegating to the active tool via a stable ref.

nodes.name: EditorPage.tsx
nodes.summary: Main editor page that orchestrates the entire 3D/2D interior design editor, managing EngineContext provisioning, mode switching (3D/2D), loading screen lifecycle, viewport sync, keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl+S save, Ctrl+O load), and custom DOM events for navigation and gizmo mode.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a file format called .homeverseplan (JSON, SceneDocument v1) for serialization; save triggers a Blob download, load uses FileReader with schema validation.

nodes.name: EditorPage
nodes.summary: Root editor page component that provides EngineContext, coordinates 3D/2D mode transitions, manages loading screen animation with engine-ready signal, listens for custom DOM events from InputSystem, and wires up save/load file handling.

nodes.name: HomePage.tsx
nodes.summary: Marketing landing page for the Tiny Home application featuring a hero section with logo and CTAs, a three-column feature grid, a community showcase gallery, and a footer, all using Tailwind utility classes with a warm earthy design system.

nodes.name: ProjectsPage.tsx
nodes.summary: Projects management page with a sidebar navigation and a searchable grid of saved project cards, displaying sample projects with thumbnails, dates, and a new-project creation card.

nodes.name: PrivateRoute.tsx
nodes.summary: Empty placeholder file for a private/authenticated route guard component.

nodes.name: routes.md
nodes.summary: Empty placeholder documentation file for the routes directory.

nodes.name: Routes.tsx
nodes.summary: Application routing configuration using React Router v6 BrowserRouter, mapping '/' to HomePage, '/project/:id' to EditorPage, and '/projects' to ProjectsPage.

nodes.summary: Empty placeholder documentation file for the services directory.

nodes.name: store.md

nodes.name: useFloorPlanStore.ts
nodes.summary: Adapter hook between the ECS engine and the Konva 2D canvas, subscribing to ECSSnapshot events and converting world-space metres into pixel-space Konva coordinates for nodes, walls, caps, rooms, dimensions, angle annotations, and furniture.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a custom Shoelace centroid algorithm for accurate room-area label placement; coordinate system maps world (x,z) metres with canvasX = worldX * 100 + vpW/2 and canvasY = worldZ * 100 + vpH/2.

nodes.name: useFloorPlanStore
nodes.summary: Subscribes to ECS snapshot events via EngineContext and returns memoized pixel-space Konva data arrays (nodes, walls, caps, rooms, dimensions, angleDimensions, furniture) recomputed only when the snapshot or viewport dimensions change.

nodes.name: computePolygonCentroid
nodes.summary: Computes the area-weighted centroid of a polygon using the Shoelace formula, with a fallback to vertex average when the polygon area is effectively zero.

nodes.name: useUIStore.ts
nodes.summary: Zustand global store managing UI state including sidebar visibility, decor catalog open state, the 2D active tool mode (select/draw/placing), furniture placement model ID, and viewport dimensions synchronized from window resize events.

nodes.name: objects.ts
nodes.summary: Defines TypeScript types and the static OBJECTS catalog array for all placeable decor items, each with an id, name, Material Symbols icon, category (Sleeping/Kitchen/Storage/etc.), GLB asset path, and object type.

nodes.name: objects.json
nodes.summary: Version 2 catalog data file defining placeable furniture objects (bath, shower door, single bed) with bounding boxes, collision boxes, top-down image URLs, material slots, and mesh-to-material bindings for the 3D renderer.
nodes.languageNotes: Each object entry defines separate boundingBox (visual), collisionBox (physics), materialSlots (editor-visible), and materialBindings (mesh-level) structures.

nodes.name: dispatcher.ts
nodes.summary: Central command dispatcher implementing the Command Pattern over ECS: the sole entry point for all floor-plan mutations, handling ENSURE_NODE, MOVE_NODE, ADD_WALL, REMOVE_WALL, MERGE_NODE, SPLIT_WALL, RESOLVE_INTERSECTIONS, UPDATE_WALL, PLACE_FURNITURE, MOVE_FURNITURE, ROTATE_FURNITURE, and DELETE_FURNITURE commands with invalidation-based deferred geometry rebuilds.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses dependency injection (DispatcherDeps bag) for testability and multiple-instance support; geometry rebuilds are deferred by removing WallPolygon components so WallGeometrySystem can batch-process them once per frame.

nodes.name: createDispatcher
nodes.summary: Factory function that accepts injected engine dependencies and returns the dispatch function, encapsulating all command handler logic for floor-plan topology mutations and furniture management.

nodes.name: EngineCommands.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the EngineCommand discriminated union type covering all possible commands the UI can dispatch to the ECS engine: node operations (ENSURE_NODE, MOVE_NODE), wall operations (ADD_WALL, REMOVE_WALL, MERGE_NODE, SPLIT_WALL, RESOLVE_INTERSECTIONS, UPDATE_WALL), and furniture operations (PLACE_FURNITURE, MOVE_FURNITURE, ROTATE_FURNITURE, DELETE_FURNITURE).

nodes.name: history.ts
nodes.summary: Implements the UndoHistory class, a snapshot-based undo/redo stack capped at 50 entries, where each entry stores a full SceneDocument taken before a transaction runs.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a dual-stack (undoStack / redoStack) pattern; any new push clears the redo branch to maintain linear history.

nodes.name: UndoHistory
nodes.summary: Manages dual undo/redo stacks holding SceneDocument snapshots; exposes push, undo, redo, canUndo, canRedo, and clear operations.

nodes.name: wallTopology.ts
nodes.summary: Provides the handleSplitWall helper that splits an existing wall entity at a new midpoint node, updating the ECS topology, node registry, AABB colliders, and mesh registry accordingly.
nodes.languageNotes: Extracted from dispatcher.ts to keep routing thin and allow independent unit testing of heavy geometry mutations.

nodes.name: handleSplitWall
nodes.summary: Splits a wall at a new node: mutates the original wall's endpoint, creates the new wall segment, rewires topology connections, and refreshes AABB colliders on all affected entities.

nodes.name: AutoAlign.ts
nodes.summary: ECS component that enables axis-aligned snapping for an entity, configuring which axes participate and the snap tolerance distance.

nodes.name: AutoAlign
nodes.summary: Component storing auto-alignment settings: enabled flag, target axes, and tolerance threshold used by alignment systems.

nodes.name: CameraOrbit.ts
nodes.summary: ECS component holding orbital camera state: radius, azimuth, polar angle, sensitivity, and target height for the orbit control system.

nodes.name: CameraOrbit
nodes.summary: Component describing orbital camera parameters used by OrbitControlSystem to position and animate the 3D viewport camera.

nodes.name: ColliderAABB.ts
nodes.summary: ECS component representing an axis-aligned bounding box collider with half-extents for width, height, and depth, used by the collision system.

nodes.name: ColliderAABB
nodes.summary: Component storing AABB half-extents (width, height, depth) for physics collision detection of walls, ground, and furniture entities.

nodes.name: Draggable.ts
nodes.summary: ECS component that marks an entity as draggable, with an optional lockY flag to constrain movement to the XZ plane.

nodes.name: Draggable
nodes.summary: Marker component enabling drag interaction on an entity; lockY constrains drag to the floor plane.

nodes.name: DynamicBody.ts
nodes.summary: ECS marker component tagging an entity as a dynamic physics body that participates in collision response.

nodes.name: DynamicBody
nodes.summary: Marker component indicating the entity is a dynamic physics participant subject to movement and collision resolution.

nodes.name: FurnitureTag.ts
nodes.summary: ECS component that tags an entity as a furniture item and stores its catalog model identifier.

nodes.name: FurnitureTag
nodes.summary: Marker component identifying a furniture entity and linking it to its catalog entry via modelId for asset loading and snapshot emission.

nodes.name: Mesh.ts
nodes.summary: ECS component that holds a reference to a Three.js Mesh object, connecting ECS entities to the Three.js scene graph.

nodes.name: Mesh
nodes.summary: Component storing a direct reference to a Three.js Mesh so render systems can retrieve and manipulate the scene-graph object per entity.

nodes.name: Model3D.ts
nodes.summary: ECS component referencing a loaded GLB model's root Object3D and its catalog modelId, optionally carrying per-material overrides for the render system.

nodes.name: Model3D
nodes.summary: Component linking an ECS entity to its loaded 3D model scene graph root, catalog ID, and optional material override map.

nodes.name: RoomGeometry.ts
nodes.summary: ECS component storing the computed polygon points and area of a detected room region for floor mesh generation and UI display.

nodes.name: RoomGeometry
nodes.summary: Component holding a room's boundary polygon and computed floor area used by room-detection and floor-mesh generation systems.

nodes.name: Selectable.ts
nodes.summary: ECS component that marks an entity as selectable and tracks its current selection state for gizmo and highlight systems.

nodes.name: Selectable
nodes.summary: Marker component enabling entity selection; the selected boolean is toggled by pick systems and read by gizmo and highlight systems.

nodes.name: SnapToGrid.ts
nodes.summary: ECS component configuring grid snapping for an entity: grid size, active axes, per-axis offsets, and an enabled toggle.

nodes.name: SnapToGrid
nodes.summary: Component encoding grid-snap parameters: resolution, axes mask, and XYZ offsets consumed by the snap system during drag operations.

nodes.name: StaticBody.ts
nodes.summary: ECS marker component tagging an entity as a static immovable physics body such as walls and the ground collider.

nodes.name: StaticBody
nodes.summary: Marker component designating an entity as a static collision body that never moves, used for walls and the infinite ground plane.

nodes.name: WallNodes.ts
nodes.summary: ECS component linking a wall entity to its start and end topology nodes and storing the wall's thickness dimension.

nodes.name: WallNodes
nodes.summary: Component referencing start/end NodeRegistry IDs and wall thickness; drives AABB recomputation when nodes move.

nodes.name: WallPolygon.ts
nodes.summary: ECS component storing the miter-cut polygon points and height for a wall, used by the 2D plan renderer to draw accurate junction shapes.

nodes.name: WallPolygon
nodes.summary: Component holding miter-cut corner polygon and wall height; computed lazily and cleared on topology change to trigger recomputation.

nodes.name: WallSize.ts
nodes.summary: ECS component storing the computed length and height of a wall entity, used by dimension annotation and serialization systems.

nodes.name: WallSize
nodes.summary: Component recording a wall's world-space length and height for use by dimension display and serialization.

nodes.name: WallTag.ts
nodes.summary: ECS component that tags an entity as a wall and stores its logical wall ID for dispatcher lookups and serialization.

nodes.name: WallTag
nodes.summary: Marker component identifying an entity as a wall and binding it to its integer wallId used throughout the dispatcher and serialization layer.

nodes.name: WorldSpaceMesh.ts
nodes.summary: ECS marker component flagging a mesh entity as already positioned in world space, signaling render systems to skip local-to-world transform application.

nodes.name: WorldSpaceMesh
nodes.summary: Marker component indicating the associated mesh is already in world space and should not be re-transformed by the render system.

nodes.name: Component.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the abstract Component base class that all ECS components must extend, enforcing a pure-data, no-logic contract.
nodes.languageNotes: The abstract class with no members acts purely as a TypeScript type anchor enabling instanceof checks and type-safe component queries in the World.

nodes.name: engine.ts
nodes.summary: The single bootstrap function createEngine() that assembles every subsystem — Three.js scene, ECS World, NodeRegistry, all systems, lighting, dispatcher, UndoHistory, and the game loop — returning a fully operational EngineInstance.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a circular instanceRef pattern to allow undo/redo closures to reference the EngineInstance before it is finalized at the bottom of the function.

nodes.name: createEngine
nodes.summary: Factory function that wires together the entire engine: creates the Three.js scene, instantiates ECS World and all game systems, sets up the render loop, undo/redo API, and returns the EngineInstance.

nodes.name: engineTypes.ts
nodes.summary: Central type declarations for the engine layer: EngineApi (public React-facing interface), EngineInstance (full engine object), and CameraPreset; contains no runtime logic.

nodes.name: EngineEvents.ts
nodes.summary: Defines all ECS snapshot types (NodeSnapshot, WallSnapshot, ECSSnapshot, FurnitureSnapshot, etc.) and the typed EngineEvents event-bus class that bridges ECS systems to the React UI layer.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a generic EngineEventMap type and Map<key, Set<handler>> for type-safe multi-subscriber event dispatch with automatic cleanup via returned unsubscribe functions.

nodes.name: EngineEvents
nodes.summary: Type-safe internal event bus supporting subscribe/unsubscribe semantics; caches the last ECSSnapshot so newly mounted components can read the current state without waiting for the next frame.

nodes.name: collisionUtils.ts
nodes.summary: Provides resolveCollisionFootprint, the single source of truth for furniture collision dimensions using a three-tier fallback: authored _col mesh, objects.json collisionBox, then visible mesh AABB.

nodes.name: resolveCollisionFootprint
nodes.summary: Resolves a furniture entity's collision footprint (width/depth/height) from a priority chain — GLB _col mesh, objects.json authoring, then visual AABB fallback — ensuring ghost preview and spawned entity always share identical dimensions.

nodes.name: FurnitureCatalog.ts
nodes.summary: Loads the objects.json furniture catalog at startup into a Map and exposes typed accessor functions for model URLs, bounding/collision boxes, top-down image URLs, and 2D footprints.

nodes.name: getCatalogItem
nodes.summary: Returns the raw catalog entry for a given modelId from the in-memory Map, or undefined if not found.

nodes.name: getCollisionBox
nodes.summary: Returns authored collision footprint dimensions from the catalog, falling back to boundingBox XZ if no explicit collisionBox is defined.

nodes.name: getFootprint2D
nodes.summary: Resolves a furniture item's 2D floor-plan footprint, always returning a usable value via a getCollisionBox-then-DEFAULT_FOOTPRINT fallback chain.

nodes.name: FurnitureFactory.ts
nodes.summary: ECS factory for spawning furniture entities in the 3D scene, supporting both procedural mesh-based and GLB model-based creation with collision footprint registration and full component attachment.
nodes.languageNotes: Exports both a mesh-based spawnFurniture and a GLB-based spawnFurnitureGLB path, with the latter performing bounding-box-aware normalization via the GLTF loader.

nodes.name: spawnFurniture
nodes.summary: Creates an ECS entity for a furniture item using procedural Three.js mesh geometry, registering the mesh and attaching physics and transform components.

nodes.name: spawnFurnitureGLB
nodes.summary: Asynchronously loads a GLB model, clones the scene graph with rotation applied, resolves the collision footprint, and registers the furniture as a fully-formed ECS entity.

nodes.name: GroundFactory.ts
nodes.summary: ECS factory that creates the ground plane entity with a Three.js mesh, adding it to the scene and attaching physics and transform components.

nodes.name: createGround
nodes.summary: Creates and registers the ground plane ECS entity, adding the Three.js mesh to the scene and binding multiple ECS components.

nodes.name: LightFactory.ts
nodes.summary: ECS factory providing ambient and directional light entity creation, each mapped to light component definitions in the ECS world.

nodes.name: WallFactory.ts
nodes.summary: ECS factory for constructing wall entities from geometric options, building the Three.js mesh and registering all wall-related ECS components including physics colliders.

nodes.name: createWall
nodes.summary: Builds a wall ECS entity from position, size, and material options, placing its Three.js mesh in the scene and registering nine ECS components including transform, collider, and wall-identity components.

nodes.name: NodeRegistry.ts
nodes.summary: Manages the registry of floor-plan graph nodes (wall endpoints), supporting creation, connection, movement, deletion, and snapshotting operations used by wall drawing and room detection.

nodes.name: NodeRegistry
nodes.summary: Central registry mapping node IDs to graph nodes that represent wall endpoints, with methods for CRUD operations, wall connectivity tracking, and serializable snapshots.

nodes.name: RoomDetection.ts
nodes.summary: Implements planar graph-based room detection using half-edge traversal and angular sorting to identify enclosed polygonal rooms from wall connections.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a half-edge data structure with angular sorting (atan2) to find minimal face cycles in the wall graph, filtering by minimum signed area to eliminate the outer infinite face.

nodes.name: RoomDetection
nodes.summary: Encapsulates room detection logic by converting the ECS wall graph into a planar half-edge structure and extracting minimal face cycles that represent enclosed rooms.

nodes.name: GLTFModelLoader.ts
nodes.summary: Provides a caching GLTF/GLB model loader with Draco decompression support, automatic bounding-box normalization, and collision node extraction from meshes suffixed with a collision tag.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a two-level cache (resolved cache + inflight promise deduplication) to avoid redundant network requests for the same model path.

nodes.name: GLTFModelLoader
nodes.summary: Caching Three.js GLTF loader that normalizes model scale, centers geometry, extracts dedicated collision bounding boxes from tagged meshes, and deduplicates in-flight loads.

nodes.name: MaterialRegistry.ts
nodes.summary: Registry for Three.js materials keyed by color and roughness, creating and caching MeshStandardMaterial instances on demand and providing bulk disposal.

nodes.name: MaterialRegistry
nodes.summary: Lazily creates and caches Three.js MeshStandardMaterial instances by composite color+roughness key, supporting bulk release of GPU resources.

nodes.name: MeshRegistry.ts
nodes.summary: Registry mapping ECS entity IDs to Three.js mesh objects, providing registration, lookup, and disposal operations that synchronize with the Three.js scene graph.

nodes.name: MeshRegistry
nodes.summary: Maintains a bidirectional link between ECS entity IDs and Three.js meshes, handling scene removal and geometry disposal on single or bulk entity destruction.

nodes.name: ModelRegistry.ts
nodes.summary: Registry mapping ECS entity IDs to Three.js Group roots for GLB models, supporting registration, retrieval, and scene-synchronized disposal.

nodes.name: ModelRegistry
nodes.summary: Manages Three.js Group roots for GLB-based furniture entities, mapping entity IDs to scene objects and providing individual and bulk disposal with scene removal.

nodes.name: deserialize.ts
nodes.summary: Reconstructs the full ECS scene state from a validated SceneDocument by dispatching wall creation, node positioning, and furniture placement commands in dependency order.

nodes.name: deserializeScene
nodes.summary: Reads a SceneDocument and drives the ECS command dispatcher to tear down existing walls and rebuild nodes, walls, and furniture entities in the correct order.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Barrel module for the serialization subsystem, re-exporting scene document types, validation utilities, and serialize/deserialize functions as the public API surface.

nodes.name: SceneDocument.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the TypeScript type structure for serialized scene documents, including versioned node, wall, and furniture records used by save/load and validation.

nodes.name: serialize.ts
nodes.summary: Extracts the current ECS world state into a structured SceneDocument by querying wall entities and furniture entities and mapping their components to plain data records.

nodes.name: serializeScene
nodes.summary: Queries all wall and furniture ECS entities, reads their transform and identity components, and assembles a versioned SceneDocument suitable for JSON persistence.

nodes.name: validate.ts
nodes.summary: Validates raw JSON against the SceneDocument schema with field-level type checking for nodes, walls, and furniture entries, returning structured error reports.

nodes.name: validateSceneDocument
nodes.summary: Validates a raw unknown value as a well-formed SceneDocument, checking version, array shapes, ID uniqueness, numeric types, and cross-references between nodes, walls, and furniture.

nodes.name: sceneSetup.ts
nodes.summary: Bootstraps the Three.js rendering context including scene, perspective camera, WebGL renderer, grid helper, and HDRI environment map loading for PBR lighting.
nodes.languageNotes: Loads an EXR environment map asynchronously via PMREMGenerator to provide physically-based ambient reflections without manual light sources.

nodes.name: createScene
nodes.summary: Initializes and returns the Three.js scene, camera, and renderer bound to the provided canvas, including grid helpers and asynchronous HDRI environment map setup.

nodes.name: systemSetup.ts
nodes.summary: Registers all ECS systems into the world in dependency order, wiring up collision, rendering, input, orbit camera, gizmo, dimension, and furniture placement systems.

nodes.name: createSystems
nodes.summary: Instantiates and registers all ECS systems into the world, configuring inter-system dependencies such as passing the collision system reference to the gizmo system.

nodes.name: CannonCollisionSystem.ts
nodes.summary: ECS system implementing Cannon.js-backed collision detection for furniture movement, providing AABB overlap testing, probe-based sweep queries, movement clamping, and static body synchronization.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a kinematic probe body technique: a temporary Cannon.js box body is shaped to the moving entity's collider and swept to test overlap against the physics world's static bodies.

nodes.name: CannonCollisionSystem
nodes.summary: Physics collision system that maintains synchronized Cannon.js bodies for static ECS entities (walls, furniture) and provides movement clamping and discrete overlap queries for drag operations.

nodes.name: CollisionDebugSystem.ts
nodes.summary: ECS debug system that visualizes collision AABB boxes as Three.js wireframe helpers in the scene, toggled by a keyboard shortcut.

nodes.name: CollisionDebugSystem
nodes.summary: Renders wireframe bounding-box overlays for all entities with a ColliderAABB component, enabling and disabling visualization via a keyboard toggle.

nodes.name: DimensionSystem.ts
nodes.summary: ECS system computing wall length dimensions and inter-wall angle dimensions from the node registry, publishing updates to a Zustand store for 2D overlay rendering.

nodes.name: DimensionSystem
nodes.summary: Reads wall and node ECS components each frame to compute metric length and angular dimensions, updating a shared store whenever values change to drive 2D overlay annotations.

nodes.name: DragGhostController.ts
nodes.summary: Manages a semi-transparent ghost clone of a furniture entity's Three.js model during gizmo drag operations, applying green/red tinting based on collision state.

nodes.name: DragGhostController
nodes.summary: Creates and manages a translucent ghost clone of a dragged GLB model, tracking its position in sync with the gizmo and applying collision-state tint via emissive color manipulation.

nodes.name: FurniturePlacementSystem.ts
nodes.summary: ECS system orchestrating the interactive furniture placement flow: loading a GLB ghost preview, tracking mouse position via raycasting, snapping to a grid, and confirming or cancelling placement.

nodes.name: FurniturePlacementSystem
nodes.summary: Coordinates the full ghost-preview furniture placement UX, loading the target GLB asynchronously, following mouse movement with grid snapping, performing collision checks, and dispatching the final PLACE_FURNITURE command.

nodes.name: GizmoSystem.ts
nodes.summary: ECS system wrapping a Three.js TransformControls gizmo for selecting, translating, and rotating furniture entities, with collision-aware movement clamping and command dispatch for undo/redo.

nodes.name: GizmoSystem
nodes.summary: Manages furniture selection and gizmo-driven move/rotate operations, integrating the collision system for safe-position enforcement and the drag ghost controller for visual feedback.

nodes.name: InputSystem.ts
nodes.summary: ECS system that listens for keyboard events and dispatches synthetic DOM CustomEvents matching a configurable shortcut table for global input routing.

nodes.name: InputSystem
nodes.summary: Translates raw keyboard events into application-level CustomEvents using a static shortcut map, preventing default browser behavior for matched shortcuts.

nodes.name: OrbitControlSystem.ts
nodes.summary: ECS system wrapping Three.js OrbitControls with smooth animated camera transitions, cursor-point zooming, horizontal pan, and double-click focus targeting.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements cursor-centric zoom by raycasting against scene objects and the ground plane to determine the world-space zoom target, then interpolates camera and target positions using easeOutCubic.

nodes.name: OrbitControlSystem
nodes.summary: Enhanced orbit camera controller that overlays smooth animated transitions on top of standard OrbitControls, supporting cursor-aware zooming, double-click focusing, and programmatic view transitions.

nodes.name: PlacementAssistSystem.ts
nodes.summary: ECS system that handles snap-to-grid and auto-alignment of dynamic (dragged) entities against static bodies during furniture placement, using cached AABB half-extents for efficient per-frame collision probing.

nodes.name: PlacementAssistSystem
nodes.summary: Queries dynamic and static body entities each frame, applies SnapToGrid quantization to the dynamic entity's transform, and then snaps the entity to the nearest non-overlapping surface on the X or Z axis using the AutoAlign tolerance.

nodes.name: RenderSystem.ts
nodes.summary: ECS system that synchronizes Three.js mesh positions and rotations from ECS Transform components, then calls the WebGL renderer each frame to draw the scene.

nodes.name: RenderSystem
nodes.summary: Iterates all entities with Transform and Mesh components, applies position and quaternion data to the underlying Three.js mesh (with special handling for WorldSpaceMesh entities), and invokes renderer.render().

nodes.name: RoomSystem.ts
nodes.summary: ECS system that detects closed room polygons from the wall topology graph using hash-based change detection, then creates or updates RoomGeometry ECS components and Three.js floor meshes for each detected room.

nodes.name: RoomSystem
nodes.summary: Hashes node positions and connections each frame; if topology changed, calls RoomDetection.findRooms() and reconciles the room entity set (create/update/destroy), rebuilding Three.js ShapeGeometry floor meshes with a light neutral material.

nodes.name: SnapshotSystem.ts
nodes.summary: ECS-to-React bridge system that collects wall, node, room, dimension, and furniture state each frame and emits a typed ECSSnapshot event via EngineEvents whenever the World revision changes, driving 2D plan view re-renders.

nodes.name: SnapshotSystem
nodes.summary: Reads World.revision for O(1) change detection; on change, queries all wall, node-cap, room, and furniture entities, assembles an ECSSnapshot (including live ColliderAABB sizes for accurate 2D furniture footprints), and emits it as a 'snapshot' event.

nodes.name: WallGeometrySystem.ts
nodes.summary: The most complex ECS system in the engine: computes miter and bevel join geometry for all walls at each junction node using a radial sort algorithm, then rebuilds Three.js ExtrudeGeometry wall and cap meshes on polygon change.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a miter-limit algorithm (similar to SVG/CSS stroke-linejoin) with per-node hash caching to avoid recomputing junction geometry when nothing has changed.

nodes.name: WallGeometrySystem
nodes.summary: Builds per-node wall lists, sorts them radially, computes miter/bevel intersection points, writes WallPolygon components, updates Three.js ExtrudeGeometry wall meshes, and manages cap-fill geometry at T/X junctions; uses a per-node hash cache to skip unchanged nodes.

nodes.name: coords.ts
nodes.summary: Pure coordinate and rotation conversion utilities mapping between the Three.js world space (metres, XZ plane) and the Konva 2D canvas space (pixels), with a constant scale factor and rotation direction adapters.
nodes.languageNotes: Intentionally free of any framework imports so it can be used in both engine and UI layers without bundling overhead.

nodes.name: worldToCanvas
nodes.summary: Converts a single world-space coordinate value (metres) to canvas pixel position by multiplying by PX_PER_WORLD and adding a pan offset.

nodes.name: canvasToWorld
nodes.summary: Inverse of worldToCanvas: converts a Konva pixel coordinate back to world-space metres by subtracting the pan offset and dividing by PX_PER_WORLD.

nodes.name: threeRotYToKonvaDeg
nodes.summary: Converts a Three.js Y-axis rotation (counter-clockwise radians) to a Konva rotation angle (clockwise degrees) by negating and converting units.

nodes.name: konvaDegToThreeRotY
nodes.summary: Inverse of threeRotYToKonvaDeg: converts a Konva clockwise degree value back to a Three.js CCW radian rotation for use in ECS Transform components.

nodes.name: wallHelpers.ts
nodes.summary: Provides the recomputeWallAABB helper that synchronously re-derives ECS wall component state (Transform centre/rotation, WallSize length, ColliderAABB half-extent) from NodeRegistry positions, called by the command dispatcher immediately after node mutations.

nodes.name: recomputeWallAABB
nodes.summary: Projects NodeRegistry canonical positions into three ECS components for a single wall entity: computes the midpoint (cx, cz) and rotY from the two endpoint nodes, updates Transform and WallSize, and writes len/2 into ColliderAABB.width (half-extent convention).

nodes.name: index.css
nodes.summary: Global stylesheet that imports Tailwind CSS, defines a full Material You design token set (colors, typography, spacing, radii), sets up base layout rules, and provides reusable utility classes and keyframe animations for the decor catalog panel.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Tailwind v4's @theme block for token registration, which is different from v3's tailwind.config.js approach.

nodes.name: main.tsx
nodes.summary: React application entry point that mounts the root App component into the DOM using React 18's createRoot API with StrictMode enabled.

nodes.name: layout.json
nodes.summary: Test fixture defining a small room layout with 5 nodes and 5 walls (including a wall-split scenario at node 5), used to seed the engine during development and testing.

nodes.name: objects.json
nodes.summary: Test fixture catalog defining 3 furniture objects (bath, shower door, single bed) with bounding boxes, collision boxes, top-down image URLs, material slots, and mesh material bindings for the furniture placement system.

nodes.name: vite.config.ts
nodes.summary: Vite build configuration enabling the React JSX transform and Tailwind CSS v4 Vite plugin, with a path alias mapping 'src' to the project source root for clean absolute imports.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: The README establishes the full picture of 3D-HomeVerse: a browser-based interior design editor with a synchronized 2D floor-plan view (Konva) and a live 3D viewport (Three.js). It documents the tech stack — React 19, Zustand, cannon-es physics, and a custom ECS engine — and maps out the layered architecture before you read a single line of source code. Start here to understand the "why" behind every architectural choice you will encounter in the tour.

tour.title: App Bootstrap
tour.description: The application boots in two steps: `main.tsx` calls React's `createRoot` to mount the root component, and `App.tsx` wraps the entire tree inside a `BrowserRouter` and hands off to the router. This thin entry layer exists purely to initialize React and the browser history API, keeping all real logic out of the root component.
tour.languageLesson: React 18's `createRoot` API enables concurrent rendering features (like Suspense and transitions). Wrapping the app in `<StrictMode>` causes every component to render twice in development, surfacing side-effects that should be idempotent — a useful sanity check for the ECS integration later.

tour.title: Routing & Pages
tour.description: The `Routes.tsx` file maps three URL paths — home, projects listing, and the editor — to their corresponding page components. `EditorPage.tsx` is the most important destination: it orchestrates the ECS engine lifecycle, switches between 2D and 3D view modes, and renders the full editor chrome. Understanding the route shape tells you which page is the beating heart of the application.
tour.languageLesson: React Router v6's `<Routes>` + `<Route>` tree uses JSX composition instead of configuration objects, making route nesting and code-splitting straightforward. The `/project/:id` segment provides the scene identity that the serialization layer later uses to load and save floor plans.

tour.title: Engine Public API
tour.description: `engineTypes.ts` defines the two key TypeScript interfaces that form the contract between the ECS engine and the React UI layer: `EngineApi` (the methods React is allowed to call) and `EngineInstance` (the full internal object that `createEngine()` returns). Knowing this boundary up front explains every pattern you will see in later steps — React never touches ECS internals directly; it only talks through this typed surface.
tour.languageLesson: This is the Facade pattern: a narrow, typed interface hides a complex subsystem. TypeScript discriminated unions on `EngineCommand` (seen in Step 9) enforce at compile time that callers can only issue valid commands, eliminating a whole class of runtime errors.

tour.title: ECS Primitives
tour.description: The ECS core is four files. `Component.ts` is the abstract base class every data bag extends, enforcing a no-logic contract. `System.ts` declares the `update(world, deltaTime)` contract every system must honour. `Query.ts` provides the efficient entity-matching utility that systems use to find their entities each frame. `World.ts` is the container that owns entity IDs, stores components in sparse Maps-of-Maps, and drives the system update loop. Everything else in the engine is built on top of these four primitives.
tour.languageLesson: Entity-Component-System separates identity (entity = plain integer ID), data (components = pure data bags), and behaviour (systems = stateless update functions). This makes it easy to add new behaviours (new system) or new data (new component) without touching existing code — a structural Open/Closed Principle.

tour.title: ECS Data Components
tour.description: Components are the data vocabulary of the engine. `Transform.ts` stores 3D position and quaternion orientation and is imported by nearly every system. `WallNodes.ts` links a wall entity to its two topology graph endpoints. `ColliderAABB.ts` defines the axis-aligned bounding box used by the collision and placement systems. These three components illustrate how different sub-domains (rendering, topology, physics) each get their own focused data bag attached to the same entity.

tour.title: Engine Bootstrap
tour.description: `engine.ts` contains the single `createEngine()` factory that assembles every subsystem in one place: Three.js scene, ECS World, NodeRegistry, command dispatcher, serialization, and the animation loop. `sceneSetup.ts` handles the Three.js-specific wiring — WebGL renderer, perspective camera, HDRI environment lighting, and grid. `systemSetup.ts` registers all 15+ ECS systems into the World in strict dependency order. Reading these three files together shows you exactly how the engine goes from zero to running.
tour.languageLesson: Registering systems in a fixed dependency order is important because the ECS update loop calls them sequentially each frame. For example, `WallGeometrySystem` must run before `RenderSystem` so that mesh data is ready when Three.js renders. This ordering replaces complex event-based synchronization.

tour.title: Engine–React Bridge
tour.description: `EngineContext.tsx` is the single most depended-upon file in the codebase (highest fan-in). It provides a React context that holds the `EngineInstance`, exposes a safe `useEngine()` hook, and a `useRequiredEngine()` variant that throws when the engine is not yet initialized. This bridge is what allows React components deep in the tree — toolbars, panels, the 2D canvas — to access engine methods without prop drilling.
tour.languageLesson: React Context solves 'prop drilling' for truly global values like the engine instance. The pattern of pairing a nullable `useEngine()` with a throwing `useRequiredEngine()` is a pragmatic type-safety trick: components that cannot function without the engine declare their dependency explicitly and fail fast during development.

tour.title: Command Dispatcher & Undo
tour.description: `EngineCommands.ts` defines the discriminated union of every mutation the UI can send to the engine — `ADD_WALL`, `MOVE_NODE`, `PLACE_FURNITURE`, and more. `dispatcher.ts` is the sole entry point for applying those commands to the ECS World, enforcing the Command Pattern. `history.ts` wraps the dispatcher with a snapshot-based undo/redo stack capped at 50 entries. Together these three files ensure every floor-plan mutation is auditable and reversible.
tour.languageLesson: TypeScript discriminated unions on `EngineCommand` (a union of objects each with a unique `type` string literal) enable exhaustive `switch` statements. The compiler will warn if a new command variant is added but not handled in the dispatcher — a compile-time completeness check.

tour.title: Key ECS Systems
tour.description: Four systems illustrate the range of work the ECS update loop performs each frame. `WallGeometrySystem.ts` is the most complex: it computes miter-join geometry for every wall junction and rebuilds Three.js meshes. `RenderSystem.ts` syncs ECS Transform data into Three.js object positions and triggers the WebGL render call. `SnapshotSystem.ts` is the React bridge: it collects all world state into a typed `ECSSnapshot` and emits it as an event so Zustand stores can update. `GizmoSystem.ts` wraps Three.js `TransformControls` to provide the 3D furniture selection gizmo.

tour.title: Entity Factories & Catalog
tour.description: Factories are the high-level constructors that assemble entities from raw commands. `WallFactory.ts` takes wall geometry options, builds a Three.js mesh, and attaches all required ECS components. `FurnitureFactory.ts` does the same for furniture, supporting both procedural meshes and GLB model loading. `FurnitureCatalog.ts` loads `objects.json` at startup, making model URLs and bounding-box data available to the placement system without hitting the disk again.

tour.title: Zustand State Stores
tour.description: `useUIStore.ts` manages the editor's UI state: which tool is active, whether the decor catalog is open, and the current view mode (2D or 3D). `useFloorPlanStore.ts` is the adapter between the ECS `SnapshotSystem` and the Konva 2D canvas — it subscribes to `ECSSnapshot` events and converts world-space coordinates into pixel-space for rendering. The clean separation between these two stores reflects the separation between UI concern (tools, panels) and data concern (floor plan geometry).
tour.languageLesson: Zustand stores are plain JavaScript closures — no providers, no context boilerplate. Components subscribe by calling the hook with a selector function; Zustand re-renders only when the selected slice changes. This makes them much faster than a single large React Context for high-frequency updates like per-frame ECS snapshots.

tour.title: 2D Floor Plan Canvas
tour.description: `PlanView2D.tsx` is the primary 2D editing surface, built on Konva. It renders walls, room fills, dimension annotations, and furniture sprites as Konva shapes, and routes all mouse events to the currently active tool. `SceneView3D.tsx` is the thin 3D counterpart — it wraps the WebGL canvas element and wires up the `onEngineCreated` callback so `EditorPage` knows when the Three.js renderer is ready. Together they implement the dual-view that is the core user experience of the editor.
tour.languageLesson: Konva uses a declarative React-like API (`<Stage>`, `<Layer>`, `<Line>`) for Canvas 2D rendering, but re-renders only the shapes that change rather than the full canvas. This is important for a floor-plan editor where individual walls need to update independently while others remain static.

tour.title: 2D Editing Tools
tour.description: `ToolBase.ts` defines the `ToolContext` type and the interface all tools must implement, establishing a consistent mouse-event contract. `DrawWallTool.tsx` handles click-to-draw wall creation with snap logic and real-time collision feedback. `PlaceFurnitureTool.tsx` shows a ghost preview image while the user positions a new furniture piece. `SelectTool.tsx` supports clicking walls and dragging node handles. `collision2D.ts` provides the SAT (Separating Axis Theorem) geometry underneath all three tools, blocking invalid placements before a command is ever dispatched.
tour.languageLesson: SAT (Separating Axis Theorem) is a fast 2D convex polygon collision test: two shapes do not overlap if a separating axis can be found along any edge normal. Running this in pixel-space on the Konva canvas (before dispatching an ECS command) creates a cheap pre-check that prevents the 3D engine from ever receiving an invalid state.

tour.title: Scene Serialization
tour.description: `SceneDocument.ts` defines the versioned TypeScript types that describe a saved scene: nodes, walls, and furniture records. `serialize.ts` queries the live ECS World and extracts its current state into that document format. `deserialize.ts` does the reverse — it reads a `SceneDocument` and reconstructs the full ECS scene by dispatching the appropriate `EngineCommands`. This round-trip is what enables save, load, and undo: any ECS state can be snapshotted and restored through a plain JSON document.
